request_state.conjecture: Beal: A^x + B^y = C^z with x,y,z >= 3 and gcd(gcd(A,B),C) = 1 has no solutions. Audit has shown three recurring failure modes in this project: conflating a residual mod-p congruence with an isogeny or l-adic statement; using a Chabauty rank bound over a base field to conclude about points of higher degree; and relabelling a GRH-conditional or heuristic result as unconditional.

obligations: Finiteness is proved; the explicit rational points are NOT yet determined
Coleman-Strassmann zero counting on the genus-8 quotient must bound the number of zeros to exactly the known trivial points
Trivial/boundary points must be separated from putative primitive solutions
candidate_A.failure_reason: U113 Part III: the Chabauty-Coleman route bounds the WRONG OBJECT. U99 proves rank_Z J^-(k) <= 2 < g = 8 over k = Q(sqrt5), giving #C^-(k) <= 9. But U105 own "degree obstruction" shows a positive integer solution yields c = i*2^(4/5), whose minimal polynomial is x^10 + 256 (verified exactly), of degree 10 over k. Solutions therefore give points of C^-(L) with [L:k] = 10, which are not elements of C^-(k). A bound on the k-rational points is silent about them, so "C^-(k) contains no points from solutions, therefore no solutions" is a non sequitur with a vacuously true premise. Closing this needs Chabauty over L (degree 20 over Q) with rank_Z J^-(L) < 8 RE-ESTABLISHED (ranks grow in extensions), or symmetric-power Chabauty / covering collections. None exists in U99, U102 or U105.
candidate_A.novelty_note: Only pool route whose finiteness is already unconditional; the residual gap is explicit point determination, not existence of a method.
extracted: rank_Z J^-(k) <= 2 < g = 8 over k=Q(sqrt5) is correct and reusable, but proves finiteness of C^-(k), NOT of the solution set
the solution field has degree exactly 10 over k with minimal polynomial x^10+256 - this pins down precisely which field a corrected Chabauty argument must work over
a Chabauty bound over a base field says nothing about points of higher degree; this failure mode should be checked in every other Chabauty claim in the project
candidate_A.claim: The weighted equation X^10 + 256 Y^10 = Z^17 has no primitive nontrivial integer solutions, established by determining the full set of rational points on the genus-8 anti-invariant quotient curve C^-/k via Chabauty-Coleman.
candidate_A.method: Genus-8 quotient of the Frey/Kummer cover; 2-descent bounding rank_Z J^-(k) <= 2 < g = 8; Coleman integration to pin down the finite point set.

candidate_B.failure_reason: U96 audit against the primary source found Theorem 5.23 requires Hypothesis 5, which fails identically for the weighted equation. The route is blocked at its stated hypotheses, not merely unfinished.
candidate_B.novelty_note: Records the specific hypothesis failure so the loop does not re-attempt Azon-style level lowering unchanged.
extracted: Hypothesis 5 of Azon Thm 5.23 is the precise failing ingredient: any replacement route must supply level lowering without it
The prime-5 local lift obligation was separately discharged in U98 and is reusable
candidate_B.claim: Level lowering in the style of Azon arXiv:2504.01967v2 Theorem 5.23 applies to the weighted equation X^10 + 256 Y^10 = Z^17 and eliminates the surviving Frey representation.
candidate_B.method: Modular level lowering over a totally real field via Breuil-Diamond Theorem 3.2.2 local lift hypotheses.

compatible.instructions: Are these two research candidates mathematically COMPATIBLE, in the sense that the objects, fields, exponents and equations they concern are the same or are related by a reduction that the project has already proved?

criteria.true: they concern the same equation, signature, curve or field, or one supplies an input the other consumes
criteria.false: they concern unrelated equations, signatures or methods, so no joint statement could be formed without inventing a new reduction

combination_value.instructions: If these two candidates were combined into a single line of attack, how much would the combination accomplish beyond what the better of the two accomplishes alone?
criteria: level 0: nothing; the combination is just the stronger candidate restated, or they are incompatible
level 1: the combination tidies bookkeeping but resolves no obligation that either one leaves open
level 2: one candidate discharges a specific open obligation recorded in the other
level 3: the combination closes a case or an infinite family that neither one closes alone

shared_failure.instructions: Would these two candidates FAIL FOR THE SAME REASON, so that combining them adds no diversity of failure mechanism and a single obstruction would defeat both?

criteria.true: both depend on the same blocked step, the same unverified citation, or the same one of the three recorded failure modes
criteria.false: they would fail for different reasons, so each provides genuine independent information
